To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
increasing the spatial variance in the target increases the spatial uncertainty of a target, which increases avoidance of a distractor cue that incurs a penalty.
increasing the spatial variance (SD) of a target distribution during a risky decision task increased selection bias away (SD) from a distractor cue and increased reaction times.
increased sensory uncertainty increased selection bias away a distractor cue that incurred a penalty and prolonged reaction time.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how humans make decisions under uncertainty.
how sensory uncertainty impacts spatial decisions.
the role of uncertainty in spatial decision-making, and how this relates to the spatial variability of actions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
increased sensory uncertainty in risky spatial decision making results in increased avoidance behavior.
the results confirm the predictions of a model of risk aversion that is dependent upon spatial uncertainty.
increasing sensory uncertainty increases the degree of avoidance during risky spatial decision-making.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the more uncertain you are about the spatial distribution of a target, the more you will avoid the region where you are most likely to receive feedback penalties.
increasing sensory uncertainty during spatial decisions increases the degree of selection avoidance, but only when selection uncertainty is also increased.
increased spatial uncertainty increases the spatial variance of selections and the degree to which risky spatial selections are biased away from feedback penalties.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the degree to which people avoid risky spatial decisions is modulated by the spatial uncertainty of sensory signals.
the degree of avoidance is modulated by the spatial variance of sensory signals.
increasing spatial uncertainty in a task increases selection variability.
